(i) nonphotonic electrons are produced in heavy ion collisions by charm quarks, (ii) the nonphotonic electrons in Au+Au are sensitive to charm baryon enhancement, and (iii) the nonphotronic electrons at 2<p<5 GeV/c in Au+Au at 200 GeV are suppressed relative to N{sup 1/3}{sub bin} scaled pp collisions.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the suppression of nonphotonic electron spectra in heavy ion collisions is not a direct measure of charm quark energy loss, but is also sensitive to charm baryon production.
the nonphotonic electrons are not a good measure of charm production in heavy ion collisions.
the enhancement of charm bays in heavy ion collisions can be a possible mechanism for the suppression of the nonphotomic electron spectrum.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the nonphotonic electrons are not an ideal probe of charm quark production in heavy ion collisions.
the nonphotonic electrons are a sensitive probe of charm baryon production.
